tools.name: autodev_scan
tools.summary: Scan a repository; returns RepoScanResult with language detection, directory structure, and git status.
tools.notes: Reads directory tree under repo_path. No LLM call needed for directory walk; agent may call git for status.

tools.name: autodev_classify_input
tools.summary: Classify free-form text as GitHub issue, PRD, brief, etc., and suggest the appropriate autodev flow.
tools.notes: May invoke LLM via InputClassifierAgent in apply mode; mock-safe.

tools.name: autodev_create_prd
tools.summary: Convert a project brief into a full PRD in Markdown format.
tools.notes: Synchronous multi-agent chain; returns Markdown string. Long-running with real LLMs.

tools.name: autodev_deliver_project
tools.summary: Run full Project Delivery flow: brief -> PRD -> architecture -> milestones -> implementation -> release check.
tools.notes: Shells out to Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI when mode=apply. In dry-run, uses mock executor. This is the highest-risk tool for unintended filesystem writes.

tools.name: autodev_run_issue
tools.summary: Run Issue Pipeline flow against an existing repo: classify, plan, and implement a fix.
tools.notes: Same shell-out risk as autodev_deliver_project. Dry-run is safe.

tools.name: autodev_report
tools.summary: Generate and return the final delivery report for a completed run.
tools.notes: Reads run state JSON from .dev-factory/runs/<run_id>/. Returns Markdown text.

tools.name: autodev_roundtable
tools.summary: Run a BMAD party-mode roundtable: N independent agents discuss a topic and synthesize a verdict.
tools.notes: Invokes real `claude` CLI subprocesses per AgentCard unless FACTORY_FORCE_MOCK=1. Can be expensive.

tools.name: autodev_release_check
tools.summary: Run a release readiness check on a completed run and return a ReleaseCheckReport.
tools.notes: Reads .dev-factory/runs/<run_id>/run_state.json. Deterministic check, no LLM call.

tools.name: autodev_list_runs
tools.summary: List recent run IDs (up to 20) for a repository with summary metadata.
tools.notes: Safest tool: pure filesystem directory listing under .dev-factory/runs/. Used as primary smoke target.

secret_leakage_detail: tools.py only accesses os.environ.get('FACTORY_FORCE_MOCK', '0') — a non-secret feature flag. No dotenv, no API key reads, no .env path access.
shell_exec_in_mcp_files: none — server.py and tools.py contain zero subprocess/shell calls. Shell-out happens inside agents called by tools.

findings.title: autodev_deliver_project and autodev_run_issue shell out when mode=apply
findings.detail: These tools call FactoryConfig.from_env() then dispatch to Codex CLI / Claude CLI subprocesses. In dry-run (default) mode, a mock executor is used and no shell-out occurs. However, any MCP client that passes mode='apply' will trigger real code execution on the server host. The MCP layer has no mode guardrail — the caller controls this entirely.
findings.recommendation: Document explicitly that mode=apply is a privileged operation. Consider enforcing a server-level env-var override (e.g. AUTODEV_MCP_MAX_MODE=dry-run) that caps the effective mode regardless of caller input.

findings.title: autodev_roundtable shells out to real claude CLI by default
findings.detail: RoundtableAgent invokes real claude CLI subprocesses per AgentCard unless FACTORY_FORCE_MOCK=1. An unauthenticated MCP caller can trigger arbitrary Claude API spending by calling autodev_roundtable without setting the mock flag.
findings.recommendation: Add AUTODEV_MCP_FORCE_MOCK server-level flag or require explicit opt-in for LLM-backed tools via a capabilities negotiation field.

findings.title: tools/call exception responses use isError=True inside result, not JSON-RPC error
findings.detail: When a tool handler raises an exception, the server returns a JSON-RPC success response (no 'error' field) with 'isError: true' in the result content. This follows MCP spec convention for tool-level errors but differs from JSON-RPC 2.0 error semantics. Clients that check only for the 'error' key at the top level will not detect handler failures.
findings.recommendation: Document this clearly in the MCP server doc. Optionally add an option to surface handler exceptions as JSON-RPC errors (code -32603) for stricter clients.

findings.title: No request size limit or timeout on the stdio loop
findings.detail: The main loop in server.py reads stdin line by line with no per-line size cap and no handler timeout. A long-running tools/call (e.g. autodev_deliver_project in apply mode) will block the entire server. Malformed oversized lines are handled safely by json.JSONDecodeError but the server has no RLIMIT guard.
findings.recommendation: Add per-handler timeout via concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor + Future.result(timeout=N) for production hardening.

verdict_rationale: All 9 tools registered and listed correctly. JSON-RPC 2.0 handshake, tools/list, tools/call, and all error paths verified and passing. No secret leakage. Caveats: mode=apply tools shell out without server-level guardrail (F-001), roundtable triggers real LLM spend by default (F-002), and there is no per-handler timeout (F-004).
